about: A rewrite of the procps tools (ps, pgrep, pidof, pmap and more) in Rust, aiming to work the same as the originals.

prs.title: pmap takes memory addresses written with 0x
prs.broken: Asking pmap for a range of memory with addresses like 0x1000 failed with a parse error. The original tool accepts them with or without the 0x.
prs.changed: I made pmap drop a leading 0x or 0X before reading an address, for a single address and both ends of a range.
prs.matters: Address ranges copied from other tools work as typed.

prs.title: pidof understands %PPID, so scripts can skip their own shell
prs.broken: Scripts check whether another copy of themselves is running with pidof -o %PPID. The Rust pidof rejected %PPID, so the check always said nothing was running.
prs.changed: pidof now reads %PPID as the process that started it, and other values as before.
prs.matters: Cron jobs and init scripts that guard against running twice work again.
